the combination of trehalose and DMA improves the motility of frozen/thaw chicken semen.
the combination of trehalose with DMA improves the quality of motion of thawed chicken semen.

the combined effect of DMA and two non-permating cryoprotectant agents, trehalos and sucrose, to improve the quality of cryopreserved chicken sperm.
the development of a new protocol for cryopreservation of avian spermatozoa.

the development of a new protocol for cryopreservation of chicken sperm based on the combined effect of permeant (DMA) and non-permeable (trehalose) cryoprotectant agents, which could be useful for the preservation of genetic resources in endangered avian species.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combination of DMA and treahlose, either alone or in combination with sucrose, is a promising strategy to improve the quality of frozen-thawed chicken sperm.
the combination of trehalose with DMA is a suitable strategy to improve sperm quality after cryopreservation.
the use of DMA and trehalsose in combination with sucrose, in a ratio of 0.1 M:0.1 M, is the best cryoprotective solution for chicken sperm.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the addition of trehalose to DMA in the freezing extender improves sperm motility after thawing, and this improvement is more evident in the presence of sucrose.
trehalose, in the presence of DMA, can be used as a cryodiluent in the freezing process of chicken semen.
trehalose and DMA are the most effective cryoprotective substances in chicken semen.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of trehalose and/or sucrose to DMA can improve the quality of frozen chicken semen, especially when trehalose is used alone.
trehalose, when used in combination with permeant cryoprotective agent (DMA), can be a promising non-permeant additive in cryodiluents for chicken semen.
the combination of trehalose and DMA could be considered as a new approach for cryopreservation in chicken.
